video_title: LIVE: Pelicans vs. Pacers Postgame Interviews 10/21/2026

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's defensive lapses and transition defense
quotes.excerpt: You give a team like this 27 fast break points, and it's what we talked about.
quotes.quote: It wasn't. That was the fourth, that was the start of it, that's what was most glaring, but there were other pieces throughout the game. Taking care of the basketball, you give a team like this 27 fast break points, and it's what we talked about, we can't have that happen. So, us being able to take care of the basketball, the pick and roll coverage with Siakam and Haliburton down the stretch, our line of communication, we've got to continue to get better there. But again, that's an elite two-man combo, we've got to be better on how we handle it and the line of communication.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on the defensive lapses against the Pacers: You give a team like this 27 fast break points and it is what we talked about, we cannot have that happen.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses the team's defensive struggles and transition defense against the Pacers.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley praises Eve's defensive performance and versatility
quotes.excerpt: I thought Eve was incredible. Everything that we're talking about him being and doing was exactly that.
quotes.quote: I thought Eve was incredible. I thought he was absolutely incredible. Everything that we're talking about him being and doing was exactly what he showed tonight. Being able to protect the rim, being able to get out in transition, in the pick and roll, covering for others, covering for guys as the low man. He did a lot of very good things for us tonight. His energy and his effort is exactly what we're going to continue to need from him on a nightly basis.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on Eve: I thought he was absolutely incredible. Everything that we are talking about him being and doing was exactly what he showed tonight.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley praises the defensive performance and versatility of Eve following the game.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the defensive challenges of starting Fears and Murray
quotes.excerpt: Those two guys are guys that can pick up full court, change the dynamic of the game.
quotes.quote: I think you have the head of the snake. Those two guys are guys that can pick up full court, change the dynamic of the game. They started out hot, it became the fouls that turned up a lot of it, and that's what happened in the fourth quarter as well. We have to understand the level of aggression we can play with, but then also when they get in that bonus, how we can be smart in our positioning and the details of where we are there.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on the starting backcourt: You have the head of the snake. Those two guys are guys that can pick up full court, change the dynamic of the game.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the defensive challenges and aggression levels when starting Fears and Murray.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the importance of turnover battle and free throws
quotes.excerpt: It's those small things and then the free throws down the stretch.
quotes.quote: They had nine offensive rebounds for 17 second chance points. We had 27 second chance opportunities. So, I think you get there, but then that's where it goes from the turnover battle. We turned over 15 times for 16 points, they turned over 12 for 16 points. So, it's those small things and then the free throws down the stretch. It was more that they ended up in the bonus faster than we needed them to be. So, I think we can be better there.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on the loss: It was more that they ended up in the bonus faster than we needed them to be. So, I think we can be better there.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley analyzes the impact of turnovers and free throws on the game's outcome.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley credits Herb Jones for his defensive impact

quotes.quote: Herb came in the game and changed the game with his defensive effort, his defensive energy, his toughness, his physicality. I think those are big keys, and taking note of that is a very big key for us.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on Herb Jones: Herb came in the game and changed the game with his defensive effort, his defensive energy, his toughness, his physicality.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Zion and Trey's need for better spacing
quotes.excerpt: There are opportunities for us to spray when we get down in the paint.
quotes.quote: That's the beauty of film. You go back, you watch it, you clean up some things that you can do. There are opportunities for us to spray when we get down in the paint when there's three in there. Zubac did a great job of being vertical at the rim, they did a very good job down there. So, finding the open man, creating the right space necessary when so we have an outlet for them when they get into the paint. So, I think we'll just have to go back and look at the film and see exactly what it looks like for our spacing for the decision making.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on spacing: There are opportunities for us to spray when we get down in the paint when there is three in there. We will have to go back and look at the film.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses the need for better spacing and decision-making for Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's defensive communication and accountability
quotes.excerpt: The guys are buying into how hard they need to play, how they have to communicate.
quotes.quote: For the most part, I think we did a pretty good job. And then there was the small breakdowns, but in games like this, you see a three-point game, those are the small things that you have to make sure you have tightened up. And so as we go back and look at the film tomorrow, being able to see how we can clean some of those things up. But the guys are buying into how hard they need to play, how they have to communicate with one another, and this is game one, but being able to understand as we move forward, how we can continue to improve and be better and continue to hold each other accountable in that regard.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on team accountability: The guys are buying into how hard they need to play, how they have to communicate with one another.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley reflects on the team's defensive communication and accountability after their first game.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Zion's confidence and shot selection
quotes.excerpt: I thought his confidence level in his shot, but his confidence level in getting to the rim.
quotes.quote: I thought he was great. I thought he was really good tonight. I thought his confidence level in his shot, but his confidence level in getting to the rim, trying to attack the basket downhill, which is one thing we know he's capable of doing. And then early on, being able to sit down and guard, being able to sit and make sure guys didn't get into the paint early. Again, what cost us in this game was the turnovers, the late transition baskets, and then our lines of communication down the stretch, which we will clean up moving forward.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on Zion Williamson: I thought his confidence level in his shot, but his confidence level in getting to the rim, trying to attack the basket downhill, was great.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley evaluates Zion Williamson's confidence, shot selection, and defensive effort.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Murray's leadership and toughness
quotes.excerpt: He's a true leader. He's a born leader.
quotes.quote: He's a true leader. He's a born leader. And I think that says a lot about him and who he is and what he wants to protect our guys. And I think for us, it has to be that night in and night out. We talk about representing this city, and there's a toughness and a grit to this city, and that's who we have to be every time we step on this floor, regardless of the circumstances, regardless who is the opponent. We have to do what we do with a level of toughness, physicality, grit, and resilience night in and night out.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on Dejounte Murray: He is a true leader. He is a born leader. We have to do what we do with a level of toughness, physicality, grit, and resilience night in and night out.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley praises the leadership and toughness displayed by Dejounte Murray.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Herb Jones' role and professionalism
quotes.excerpt: Herb is the ultimate pro.
quotes.quote: Herb is the ultimate pro. And those conversations that we have, understanding that the minutes and how he plays is he's asking what he needs to do night in and night out. He's going to be a doggish defender night in and night out, stepping into a shot, knocking it down when need be. But he, he's the ultimate pro and he's actually a coach's dream to be to be able to communicate at a high level with him for what he sees, how he understands the game, and what he knows is going on within the game.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on Herb Jones: Herb is the ultimate pro. He is actually a coach's dream to be able to communicate at a high level with him.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley describes Herb Jones as the ultimate professional and a coach's dream.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's committee-based approach
quotes.excerpt: We've always talked about it being done by committee.
quotes.quote: That's a great question. That is a really good question. And with us, we've always talked about it being done by committee. And some nights it's going to be one, some nights it's going to be another, because the matchups will change. And how we get them into those situations will determine exactly how we're being matched up against. You know, Z had a big on him and then we try to put Haliburton in the pick and roll with the switch. They did a great job of getting back over it, but it is not just the responsibility of the one four or two four, whoever it is. Whoever has that ball in their hands, you are now the playmaker to make everyone else around you better, whether you get the shot or you distribute it to somebody on the perimeter to now make the next play. But that's the beauty of this group, because we have a lot of guys that can do that.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on the team's offensive approach: We have always talked about it being done by committee. Whoever has that ball in their hands, you are now the playmaker.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the team's committee-based approach to playmaking and defensive matchups.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's need to play the right way
quotes.excerpt: It's about playing the right way with each other.
quotes.quote: I think there's an opportunity for each guy to establish how they can help us get the result that we're looking for within games if we're playing the right way. Because I think even if it's Z getting the ball at the end of the game, his job and responsibility to this team is if he gets down hill and then somebody's there, he's spraying it out so now we have a knockdown three. So whatever it looks like, it's about playing the right way with each other, because everybody can have an opportunity in that.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on team play: It is about playing the right way with each other, because everybody can have an opportunity in that.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley emphasizes the importance of playing the right way and making the extra pass.

quotes.speaker: Zion Williamson
quotes.summary_phrase: Zion Williamson on the team's missed execution and turnovers
quotes.excerpt: Just down the line, we didn't execute. The turnovers throughout the game caught up to us.
quotes.quote: You know, we gave ourselves a chance. We gave ourselves a chance to win. We just down the line, we didn't execute. The turnovers throughout the game caught up to us. Their transition points as well, I want to say they had 27. Like 25, 27 transition points. Um, and then late in the game, uh, we just got to execute. Like, I got to get the shots we want, just like they got the shots they want. We just got to get the shots we want, at least get the shot off, and we just can't turn it over.
quotes.social_post: Zion Williamson on the loss: We gave ourselves a chance to win. We just down the line, we didn't execute. The turnovers throughout the game caught up to us.

structured.context: Zion Williamson discusses the team's missed execution and turnovers in the final moments of the game.
